title: The Call of Cthulhu by H. P. Lovecraft

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator frames the dangers of correlating scientific knowledge, warning that piecing together dissociated data will reveal terrifying realities.
evidence.quote: We live on a placid island of ignorance in the midst of black seas of infinity, and it was not meant that we should voyage far. The sciences, each straining in its own direction, have hitherto harmed us little; but some day the piecing together of dissociated knowledge will open up such terrifying vistas of reality

evidence.paraphrase: Professor Angell interrogates Wilcox methodically and studies the bas-relief with intense analytical attention.
evidence.quote: He questioned the sculptor with scientific minuteness; and studied with almost frantic intensity the bas-relief on which the youth had found himself working

evidence.paraphrase: The professor systematically collected dream reports and dates from many people to compile a data digest.
evidence.quote: My uncle, it seems, had quickly instituted a prodigiously far-flung body of inquiries amongst nearly all the friends whom he could question without impertinence, asking for nightly reports of their dreams, and the dates of any notable visions for some time past.

evidence.paraphrase: Wilcox dreams of an immense alien city of massive blocks and monoliths covered in green ooze.
evidence.quote: he had had an unprecedented dream of great Cyclopean cities of Titan blocks and sky-flung monoliths, all dripping with green ooze and sinister with latent horror

evidence.paraphrase: Legrasse and Webb compare ritual chants from geographically distant cults and find them nearly identical.
evidence.quote: There then followed an exhaustive comparison of details, and a moment of really awed silence when both detective and scientist agreed on the virtual identity of the phrase common to two hellish rituals so many worlds of distance apart.

evidence.paraphrase: The statuette's material is described as unrecognizable to known geology or mineralogy.
evidence.quote: the soapy, greenish-black stone with its golden or iridescent flecks and striations resembled nothing familiar to geology or mineralogy

evidence.paraphrase: The cult explains that ancient beings, the Great Old Ones, came from the sky before humanity and now lie hidden inside earth and sea.
evidence.quote: They worshiped, so they said, the Great Old Ones who lived ages before there were any men, and who came to the young world out of the sky. Those Old Ones were gone now, inside the earth and under the sea

evidence.paraphrase: Castro explains the Old Ones' non-material composition and their dependence on stellar alignment for movement between worlds and survival.
evidence.quote:
These Great Old Ones, Castro continued, were not composed altogether of flesh and blood. They had shape
did not this star-fashioned image prove it?
but that shape was not made of matter. When the stars were right, They could plunge from world to world through the sky; but when the stars were wrong, They could not live.

evidence.paraphrase: The Old Ones communicate via transmitted thought and remain aware of the universe from their tombs.
evidence.quote: They knew all that was occurring in the universe, for Their mode of speech was transmitted thought. Even now They talked in Their tombs.

evidence.paraphrase: Castro predicts a future when humans become like the Old Ones, abandoning morals and descending into violent revelry.
evidence.quote: The time would be easy to know, for then mankind would have become as the Great Old Ones; free and wild and beyond good and evil, with laws and morals thrown aside and all men shouting and killing and reveling in joy.

evidence.paraphrase: The story contrasts ordinary geometry with the non-Euclidean, alien spatial properties experienced both in dreams and in reality.
evidence.quote: the geometry of the dream-place he saw was abnormal, non-Euclidean, and loathsomely redolent of spheres and dimensions apart from ours. Now an unlettered seaman felt the same thing whilst gazing at the terrible reality.

evidence.paraphrase: The sailors discover the risen sunken city of R'lyeh as a physical place emerging from the sea.
evidence.quote:
in S. Latitude 47
come upon a coastline of mingled mud, ooze, and weedy Cyclopean masonry which can be nothing less than the tangible substance of earth's supreme terror
the nightmare corpse-city of R'lyeh

evidence.paraphrase: At R'lyeh the visual environment and angles behave in distorted, impossible ways.
evidence.quote: The very sun of heaven seemed distorted when viewed through the polarizing miasma welling out from this sea-soaked perversion, and twisted menace and suspense lurked leeringly in those crazily elusive angles of carven rock where a second glance showed concavity after the first showed convexity.

evidence.paraphrase: The gigantic creature Cthulhu emerges from the opened door of the city.
evidence.quote: It lumbered slobberingly into sight and gropingly squeezed Its gelatinous green immensity through the black doorway into the tainted outside air of that poison city of madness.

evidence.paraphrase: After immense spans of time, Cthulhu is freed and active.
evidence.quote: After vigintillions of years great Cthulhu was loose again, and ravening for delight.

evidence.paraphrase: A sailor, Briden, goes insane after seeing Cthulhu and laughs until he dies.
evidence.quote: Briden looked back and went mad, laughing shrilly as he kept on laughing at intervals till death found him one night in the cabin

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator describes his permanent dread and expectation of early death after learning the truth.
evidence.quote: I have looked upon all that the universe has to hold of horror, and even the skies of spring and the flowers of summer must ever afterward be poison to me. But I do not think my life will be long.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator contrasts human mental limitation with the hidden totality of reality, treating ignorance as protective.
evidence.quote: the most merciful thing in the world, I think, is the inability of the human mind to correlate all its contents

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator warns of a future when the hidden horror will return and human civilization decays.
evidence.quote:
Loathsomeness waits and dreams in the deep, and decay spreads over the tottering cities of men. A time will come
but I must not and can not think!

evidence.paraphrase: Scientific experts examine the idol's stone and conclude it matches no known rock on earth.
evidence.quote: Geologists, the curator told me, had found it a monstrous puzzle; for they vowed that the world held no rock like it.

evidence.paraphrase: The crew lands on an island that reportedly does not exist on any chart of that ocean region.
evidence.quote: The next day, it appears, they raised and landed on a small island, although none is known to exist in that part of the ocean
